title: How Well Do You Know Moses?
subtitle: From the basket to the burning bush to the Promised Land.

questions.text: As a baby, where was Moses hidden to save his life?

options.explanation: Caves shelter others in the Bible, but baby Moses was hidden in the river.

options.text: In a basket among the reeds of the Nile
options.explanation: His mother placed him in a basket coated with pitch and set it among the reeds (Exodus 2:3).
There was no temple yet in Moses' day, and he was hidden by the river.
Wells matter in other Bible stories, but Moses was floated on the Nile in a basket.

questions.text: Who found baby Moses and raised him?

options.explanation: Moses grew up in the palace, not on a farm.
Pharaoh's daughter found him at the river and raised him as her own son (Exodus 2:5-10).
Aaron was Moses' brother, but a princess drew him from the water.
Moses met shepherds in Midian much later, as a grown man fleeing Egypt.

questions.text: From what did God speak to call Moses to lead Israel?

options.explanation: The pillar of cloud led Israel later in the wilderness, after the exodus began.
God spoke to Job from a whirlwind, but Moses was called from a bush.
The bush was on fire yet not burned up, and God called to Moses from inside it (Exodus 3:2-4).
A star guided the wise men to Jesus, not Moses to his calling.

questions.text: Who did God send to be Moses' spokesman before Pharaoh?

options.explanation: Moses felt slow of speech, so God sent his brother Aaron to speak for him (Exodus 4:14-16).
Joshua was Moses' helper and successor, but Aaron was the spokesman.
Miriam was Moses' sister and a prophetess, but Aaron spoke before Pharaoh.
Caleb was a faithful spy later on, not Moses' spokesman.

questions.text: How many plagues did God send on Egypt?

options.explanation: Seven is close, but the full count of plagues was higher.
Ten plagues struck Egypt, ending with the death of the firstborn (Exodus 7 through 12).
Twelve matters for the tribes of Israel, but the plagues numbered ten.
There were far more than three. Egypt suffered ten plagues in all.

questions.text: What was the final plague that made Pharaoh let Israel go?

options.explanation: Locusts were one of the plagues, but not the last one.
Hail came earlier in the sequence, not at the end.
The tenth plague struck down the firstborn of Egypt, and that is when Pharaoh let Israel go (Exodus 12:29-31).
Frogs were an early plague, far from the final one.

questions.text: What body of water did God part so Israel could escape Egypt on dry ground?

options.explanation: The Jordan was parted later, under Joshua, as Israel entered the Promised Land.
God parted the Red Sea, and Israel walked across on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22).
The Sea of Galilee belongs to the Gospel stories of Jesus, not the exodus.
The Dead Sea is not where the crossing happened. It was the Red Sea.

questions.text: On what mountain did Moses receive the Ten Commandments?

options.explanation: Mount Carmel is where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal, much later.
Mount Nebo is where Moses later viewed the Promised Land, not where he got the Law.
Moses received the commandments on Mount Sinai, also called Horeb (Exodus 19 and 20).
Mount Zion is tied to Jerusalem in later Scripture, not to the giving of the Law.

questions.text: What did the Israelites make and worship while Moses was on the mountain?

options.explanation: The bronze serpent came later as a means of healing, not as an idol they crafted here.
While Moses was away, the people made a golden calf and worshiped it (Exodus 32:1-4).

options.text: A stone altar to the true God
options.explanation: This was idolatry, not faithful worship. They made a golden calf.
There was no silver throne. The idol they made was a golden calf.

questions.text: How many years did Israel wander in the wilderness?

options.explanation: It was longer than ten years in the wilderness.
Israel wandered forty years until that generation had passed (Numbers 14:33-34).
Seven years is too short for the wilderness journey, which lasted forty.
A hundred years is far too long. The wandering lasted forty years.

questions.text: Did Moses himself enter the Promised Land?

options.text: No, he saw it from a mountain but did not enter
options.explanation: Moses viewed the land from Mount Nebo but died there without crossing in (Deuteronomy 34:1-5).

options.text: Yes, he led the people across the Jordan
options.explanation: Joshua led the people across the Jordan. Moses had already died.
Moses never settled in the land. He only saw it from a distance.

options.text: No, he turned back to Egypt instead
options.explanation: Moses did not return to Egypt. He died in the land of Moab, in sight of Canaan.

scoring.perfectMessage: You know the life of Moses like a true guide.

gradeBands.label: Wanderer
gradeBands.message: A good moment to revisit Exodus and the journey of Moses.

gradeBands.label: Traveler
gradeBands.message: You know the main stops on Moses' road.

gradeBands.label: Guide
gradeBands.message: You know the story of Moses very well.

gradeBands.label: Deliverer
gradeBands.message: Incredible. You could lead the tour from the Nile to Nebo.
